title: Hybrid delta per-token pricing pilot with streaming uplift cap and SQ onboarding checklist
creator: Priyanka Shah
description:
Hypothesis: Introducing a hybrid per-token delta pricing model (distinct ingress/output rates with a capped streaming uplift) will better align customer costs with resource usage patterns and reduce overbilling complaints from conversational customers while preserving revenue for high-output workloads. We expect: (1) short-turnaround chat apps (many small outputs) will see net-neutral to slightly lower bills due to capped streaming uplift, (2) batch/translation customers (high output per request) will shift toward output-weighted pricing which better reflects compute cost.

Experiment overview: Create a pilot gated to new signups and opt-in enterprise customers that applies: - Input tokens billed at base_input_rate, Output tokens billed at base_output_rate (output rate > input rate). - For streamed responses, apply a streaming uplift multiplier up to a hard cap per-session (stream_uplift_cap_tokens) to prevent runaway streaming surcharges. - Provide a billing preview in Console and per-account telemetry to compare baseline vs hybrid delta billing.

Success metrics: Primary: revenue per request class (chat/session, batch, embeddings) and net MRR impact across cohorts. Secondary: number of billing support tickets related to token confusion, usage of streaming cap opt-out, customer satisfaction score for pilot cohort. Operational metrics: billing accuracy rate, lag in invoice generation, telemetry event coverage >= 95%.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Backend billing pipeline supports separate input/output token counters and applies per-session streaming uplift cap. 2) Console displays an itemized cost preview (input/output/stream-uplift) for pilot customers. 3) Telemetry events emitted for every request with token breakdown and stream flag. 4) Sales + Legal SQ checklist completed for enterprise pilots. 5) Rollout toggles exist for region, customer tier, and opt-in/opt-out. 6) No more than 1% invoices in the pilot cohort require manual adjustment after first full billing cycle.
updates: 2025-02-12: Kickoff with Eng (SRE and Billing) and Research to validate token classification and latency implications.
2025-02-18: Finance model draft completed; baseline vs delta scenarios simulated on last 90d traffic sample. Initial projection: +4% gross rev for batch-heavy accounts, -2% for conversational-heavy.
2025-02-24: Design working on Console cost-preview wireframes (mock link in links). Need copy review for customer-facing explanations.
2025-03-03: Legal requested SQ artifact: detailed data flow diagram + retention policy and KMS usage note. Owner: Security (Asha Rao) assigned.
2025-03-08: Engineering spike estimated 2.5 sprints; POC telemetry event schema proposed and reviewed by infra. Billing pipeline schema changes scoped.
2025-03-12: PM decision: pilot to target 50 new signups + 5 enterprise opt-ins. Next: finalize SQ checklist, permute pricing band thresholds for AB test groups.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: internal validation with synthetic traffic (2 weeks). Phase 1: opt-in enterprise pilot (5 customers) + 50 new self-serve signups (4 weeks). Phase 2: expand to 20% of new signups with AB analysis (6 weeks). Each phase gated by billing accuracy and SQ/legal clearance. De-risking: default fallback to existing uniform per-token pricing on mismatch or customer request.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: confusion leading to increased billing disputes. Mitigation: console cost-preview + in-console educational tooltip + proactive email for pilot customers. Risk: invoice generation delays due to new counters. Mitigation: double-run billing job for first month and automated reconciliation alerts. Risk: SQ objections on telemetry. Mitigation: redact PII in telemetry and provide detailed SQ artifact to Security and Legal.
